fixture_method: Python extracts exact function bodies by signature from pinned bot.cpp, rejecting any source SHA mismatch; C++ compiles those unchanged bodies against declared deterministic mocks for world/native/helper interfaces.
coverage_cases: scalar initialization before early spawn return
outmatched scalar records pack=true plus paying_soon=true
outmatched with pack=false leaves the initialized scalar false
safe positive pack-suppression finishing recall: keep, cached home stays false, one stand evaluation, single contextual threat/tribute/outruns checks
own winning top-up declines contextual exception using mocked capture_share/gems_short outputs
pending allied tribute decisive top-up declines using mocked capture_share/gems_short outputs
game-ending enemy intervention cancels before want_home/context work
no pack-suppression case does not enter contextual branch
payout not early delegates to capture_recall; mocked capture_recall=true remains authoritative
recall-outruns failure declines contextual exception and preserves home=false
normal home=true path remains unchanged, including priority over winning top-up
not holding a capture bypasses new branch

mutations: game-ender branch suppressed while still calling game_ender

call_count_checks: Fixture asserts production stand count and order-sensitive threat, tribute, outruns, game_ender, pack/paying, capture share/short, stale-check, and cancel/capture_recall calls for each case. Positive uses one stand in want_home and does not trigger a second stand in the exception.
scope_limits: The test compiles exact production bodies for outmatched, want_home, and continue_recall only.
World, native reads, Safety, game_ender, capture_recall, tribute safety, recall-outruns, and other adjacent helpers are deterministic mocks; this is not native integration.

capture_share and gems_short are mocked inputs; the fixture tests the production comparison/control flow, not allied tribute accounting or actual winning-top-up classification. The pending-tribute test is named accordingly.
It does not show that runtime private state in the recorded game equals fixture values or establish competitive benefit.
